title_en: Typical Cases of the Supreme People's Court on Giving Full Play to the Role of Intellectual Property Adjudication Functions to Promote the Great Development and Prosperity of Socialist Culture and to Promote Independent and Coordinated Economic Development
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Typical Cases concerning Full Play of the Role of Intellectual Property Adjudication Functions in Promoting the Great Development and Prosperity of Socialist Culture and Facilitating the Coordinated Development of Economic Autonomy

1. Appeal Cases concerning Universal Music Group, Warner Music Group, and Sony Music Entertainment v. Baidu Inc. for Copyright Infringement

Appeal Cases concerning Universal Music Limited, Warner Music Limited, Sony Music Entertainment Hong Kong Limited v. Beijing Baidu Netcom Science Technology Co., Ltd. for Copyright Infringement (Civil Mediation Documents No. 1694, 1700, 1699 of the Beijing High People's Court, Final instance; Civil Judgments (2008) Yi Zhong Min Chu Zi Nos. 5043, 5026, 5154 of the Beijing First Intermediate People's Court)

[Summary of Facts]

Universal Music Group, Warner Music Group, and Sony Music Entertainment discovered that 128 songs to which they held sound recording producer rights were linked and provided with online playback and download services through the MP3 section of Baidu's website, via search boxes, charts, and other modes. The three record companies claimed that Baidu's above actions infringed their right of communication to the public via information networks, and requested the court to order Baidu to compensate them for economic losses and reasonable expenses totaling RMB 63.5 million. After trial, the court of first instance held that Baidu's service of conducting searches and establishing temporary links based on instructions from network users was automatic and passive in nature. Even if Baidu exercised a degree of care commensurate with its capacity, it would be difficult for it to know whether the information involved in its service infringed rights. Therefore, neither the setting up of a search box for network users to enter keywords to search for songs nor the setting up of charts and other modes could prove that Baidu knew or should have known that the linked sound recordings were infringing. Accordingly, Baidu did not constitute infringement of the right of communication to the public via information networks, and the court rejected all claims of the three major record companies. The three major record companies appealed. During the second-instance trial, the collegiate bench, after holding two public hearings and accurately ascertaining the facts, and with the cooperation of the Mediation Center of the Internet Society of China, carried out substantial mediation efforts, ultimately leading the parties to conclude a settlement agreement based on a fundamental cooperation agreement regarding the disputes involved. The settlement agreement confirmed that the parties would jointly commit to innovation in the operational models for Internet music works and innovation in the copyright protection models for Internet music works, and would engage in comprehensive cooperation. They signed a cooperation agreement and an anti-piracy agreement concerning the specific methods and content of the comprehensive cooperation. Baidu and the three major record companies also reached an agreement under which Baidu would pay royalties, and the three major record companies would authorize Baidu to upload their entire song catalogues and forthcoming new song catalogues; network users could directly access Baidu's website for free online playback and download of the relevant songs. Thus, the long-standing copyright disputes between Baidu and the three major record companies were completely resolved, and hundreds of millions of netizens could thereafter access a large number of legitimate songs on Baidu's website.

[Typical Significance]

With the rapid development of network technology and the network industry, online playback and downloading of music works have become the main means for people to enjoy music works. However, there are still many instances of unauthorized dissemination of works on the Internet. The successful mediation of this case not only properly resolved the disputes but also enabled the rights holders and the users of the works to reach a long-term cooperation, effectively curbing "online piracy," fundamentally safeguarding the legitimate rights and interests of the rights holders, greatly stimulating their enthusiasm for creation, and at the same time allowing hundreds of millions of netizens to enjoy legitimate music works, thereby effectively achieving a balance between the interests of rights holders and the public. The successful mediation of this case is a concrete manifestation of the people's courts' efforts to promote the healthy and orderly development of new cultural industries in the Internet era.

2. Confirmation of Non-infringement of Trademark Rights between Hongtaiyang Company and Jianghuai Group and Jianghuai Co., Ltd.

Application for Retrial concerning Guangzhou Hongtaiyang Motor Vehicle Accessories Co., Ltd. v. Anhui Jianghuai Automobile Group Co., Ltd. and Anhui Jianghuai Automobile Co., Ltd. for Confirmation of Non-infringement of Exclusive Trademark Rights (Civil Order (2011) Min Shen Zi No. 223 of the Supreme People's Court)

[Summary of Facts]

From 2005 onward, Jianghuai Group and Jianghuai Co., Ltd. used an oval shape with a five-pointed star logo on the automobiles they produced, and carried out extensive and continuous publicity, gaining a certain degree of recognition. This oval shape with a five-pointed star logo was applied for registration in 2005 but was not approved, and thus constituted an unregistered trademark. Hongtaiyang Company applied for Trademark Nos. 4233581 and 4425670 to the Trademark Office of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce in 2004, and these were approved for registration in 2007 in Class 12 for automobiles. In 2010, Hongtaiyang Company and related enterprises began large-scale media promotion of these registered trademarks. On March 26, 2010, Hongtaiyang Company sent a lawyer's letter to Jianghuai Co., Ltd., urging it to respect Hongtaiyang's intellectual property rights and not to infringe its exclusive trademark rights. After receiving the lawyer's letter, Jianghuai Group filed a lawsuit with the Hefei Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province seeking confirmation of non-infringement of the registered trademark rights, and later Jianghuai Co., Ltd. joined the lawsuit. The Hefei Intermediate People's Court rendered a first-instance judgment on September 13, 2010, holding that the trademarks of the parties were not similar and therefore Jianghuai Group and Jianghuai Co., Ltd. did not infringe Hongtaiyang's registered trademark rights. Hongtaiyang Company appealed. The Anhui High People's Court rendered a second-instance judgment on October 29, 2010, affirming the first-instance judgment. Dissatisfied with that judgment, Hongtaiyang Company applied to the Supreme People's Court for retrial. Because the case involved multiple related civil and administrative dispute cases and administrative controversies, under the auspices of the Supreme People's Court, the parties voluntarily reached a settlement agreement, resolving all their lawsuits and disputes in a package.

[Typical Significance]

This case primarily involved issues such as the determination of trademark similarity, and the facts were not particularly complex. However, because it involved two large automobile enterprises with multiple related civil and administrative lawsuits and administrative disputes between them, its social impact was significant. A direct judgment concluding the case would not thoroughly resolve the disputes between the parties, whereas a settlement agreement would be conducive to the development and cooperation of each enterprise. Therefore, based on the facts ascertained and the rights and wrongs clarified, the Supreme People's Court, in accordance with the specific circumstances of the case, correctly applied the working principle of "mediation first, combining mediation with adjudication" to facilitate the parties in reaching a settlement agreement. Each party withdrew multiple lawsuits, completely resolving the conflicts between them and achieving inclusive growth and harmonious development.
